items.note: Dodd 2017 Nature, Papineau 2022 Sci Adv (sample coordinates N58°16'50.9" W77°44'14.7"), Québec stratigraphic lexicon for the dating dispute. On Inukjuak Inuit land in Nunavik; include Inuktitut names.

Separation of India from Madagascar
items.note: Gibbons et al. 2013 (94–84 Ma, south to north) vs Gilbert et al. 2024 (c. 83 Ma); Madagascar volcanics 88 Ma (Storey et al. 1995). Sets up Madagascar's isolated biota. Indian Ocean and Africa are under-covered in deep time.

items.title: Ediacaran–Cambrian boundary succession of the Nama Group, Namibia
items.note: Linnemann et al. 2019 (Terra Nova, doi 10.1111/ter.12368) date the boundary at 538.6–538.8 Ma and the Ediacaran-to-Cambrian faunal turnover to under 410 kyr in southern Namibia; an under-recorded African deep-time anchor.

items.title: Kheseen Biota, Mongolia
items.note: Exceptionally preserved assemblage deposited ~550–526 Ma, discussed as a test of molecular-clock calibrations (Science Advances 2026, doi 10.1126/sciadv.aeg6289, PMC13632735). Under-recorded Central/East Asian deep-time locality.

items.title: Emu Bay Shale Lagerstätte, Kangaroo Island, South Australia
items.note: Early Cambrian soft-tissue deposit cited alongside Burgess Shale, Chengjiang and Sirius Passet (Kihm et al. 2023, PMC10334802); fills the Oceania × Paleozoic cell. Age needs checking against primary literature.

items.title: Bright Angel Formation biota, Grand Canyon
items.note: Middle Cambrian (~507–502 Ma) carbonaceous mesofossils showing evolutionary escalation in shallow water (Mussini et al. 2025, Science Advances, PMC12285723).

items.title: Jebel Irhoud (Middle Stone Age hominin site, Morocco)
Omo Kibish Formation (Omo I and Omo II, Ethiopia)
Florisbad spring site and hominin cranium (South Africa)
Onset of the Middle Stone Age in Africa
Herto Homo sapiens fossils (Middle Awash, Ethiopia)
Middle Pleistocene green Sahara episodes
items.note: Richter et al. 2017 cite a marked but short humid episode around 330 ka enabling north/sub-Saharan continuity; needs the underlying paleoclimate source (their ref. 29) and a sea-core dataset.

items.title: Denisovans
items.note: Asian archaic population; Prüfer et al. 2014 (PMC4031459): Denisova Cave sublayer 11.2 c. 50,300 years ago, ≥0.5% Neanderthal DNA, Denisovan ancestry ~25x higher in Papuans and Australians than in mainland Asians. Strong Oceania/Asia coverage value; check later finds outside the Altai.

items.title: Shanidar Cave Neanderthal burials, Iraqi Kurdistan
items.note: Western Asian Neanderthal site, under-recorded region; burial-practice debate (the Smithsonian page mentions graves marked with offerings such as flowers). Dates not yet verified; year is a placeholder to be sourced.

items.title: Uluzzian technocomplex, earliest dated modern human industry in Europe
items.note: Italy and Greece; early dates of about 45,000 years and shell beads (Oxford/Tübingen release 2014; Douka 2011 work). Attribution to modern humans debated.

items.title: Gorham's Cave Complex, Gibraltar
items.note: UNESCO WHC 1500 (2016), N36 7 21.61 W5 20 31.42, four caves, ~120,000 years of Neanderthal and early modern human occupation, engravings older than 39,000 years. Place record needs a model if importance ≥ 3.

items.title: Phlegraean Fields caldera eruption, c. 39,850 years ago
items.note: Zilhão et al. 2017 (PMC5696381) give 39,850 years ago and link it to the Ebro barrier; check its proposed role in Neanderthal decline.

Kuk Early Agricultural Site
items.note: Independent invention of farming in highland New Guinea: mounds for banana, taro and yam c. 7,000–6,400 years ago, ditch drainage from 4,000 BP, possibly from 10,000 BP. UNESCO WHC 887 (S5 47 1.36 E144 19 54.2, 116 ha, 1,500 m). Needs Denham et al. 2003 (Science) for dates; place record importance >= 3 needs a model. Under-recorded Pacific.

items.title: Pearl millet domestication in the West African Sahel
items.note: Fully domesticated pearl millet in the Lower Tilemsi Valley, Mali, as early as 2500 BC, unambiguous by 2000 BC; eastern Mauritania by 1700 BC; dispersal to India by end of 3rd millennium BC (Winchell et al. 2018, Afr Archaeol Rev, open access at UCL Discovery; Manning et al. 2011). Pair with sorghum in the eastern Sahel (Butana Group).

items.title: Early farming in the Ñanchoc Valley, northern Peru
items.note: Squash (9240 ± 50 14C BP seeds), peanut, Phaseolus beans and pacay; farming system in place by ca. 8,600 cal BP (Piperno & Dillehay 2008 PNAS, PMC2604935; Dillehay et al. 2007 Science). Andes before 1492 is under-recorded.

items.title: Plant domestication in eastern North America
items.note: Indigenous domestication of squash (Phillips Spring, MO, 5,025 cal BP), sunflower (Hayes, TN), marshelder (Napoleon Hollow, IL) and chenopod (Cloudsplitter, KY, 3,700 cal BP) (Smith 2006 PNAS, PMC1567861; Smith & Yarnell 2009 on the crop complex at 3800 BP). Indigenous peoples of the Americas before 1492.

items.title: Rice domestication in the Lower Yangtze (Shangshan)
items.note: Phytolith-dated rice at Shangshan (29°27′21.6″N 119°58′15.4″E) from 9,400 cal BP, Hehuashan, Huxi (Zuo et al. 2017 PNAS, PMC5488950). Shangshan culture c. 11,000–8,600 cal BP.

items.title: Çatalhöyük
items.note: Neolithic settlement in central Anatolia, c. 7100–5950 cal BCE, peak population 3,500–8,000; health, workload and violence data (Larsen et al. 2019 PNAS, PMC6601267). UNESCO listing number to verify. Needs a model (place, importance >= 3).

items.title: Maize domestication in the Central Balsas Valley
items.note: Maize and squash at Xihuatoxtla shelter (964 m, near Iguala, Guerrero) by 8,700 cal BP; progenitor Balsas teosinte (Piperno et al. 2009 PMC2664021; Ranere et al. 2009 PMC2664064). Site coordinates still needed.

items.title: Inscribed tags and jars of Tomb U-j, Abydos
items.note: Earliest known Egyptian writing: nearly 200 bone/ivory tags and 125 ink inscriptions, c. 3320 BCE (calibrated 14C, Boehmer, Dreyer and Kromer 1993; questioned by Hendrickx 2006). Sources: Visible Language chs. 5-6 (MacArthur, Stauder); Dreyer 1998 (DAI); Dee et al. 2013 (PMC3780825). Umm el-Qaab GeoNames 13535544 / OSM way 90456103.

items.title: Shang oracle-bone inscriptions at Anyang
items.note: Divination records of the last nine Shang kings, c. 1220-1050 BCE (Shaughnessy, Visible Language ch. 14); UNESCO WHC 1114 Yin Xu; Wu Ding and Consort Fu Hao divinations (a woman with a known tomb, 1975/76 discovery) could be a separate person record.

items.title: Early Zapotec glyphic inscriptions at San José Mogote and Monte Albán
items.note: Monument with two glyphs at San José Mogote dated by 14C to c. 600 BCE; Monte Albán writing c. 500-200 BCE (Palka, Visible Language ch. 15). Dating is debated; needs primary site reports (Marcus and Flannery) and coordinates for the archaeological site itself, not the village.

items.title: Early Maya writing at San Bartolo
items.note: Sub-V block text 300-200 BCE by AMS 14C (Saturno, Stuart and Beltrán, Science 2006); Las Pinturas murals c. 100 BCE. science.org returns 403; try the San Bartolo project copy or Peabody/Harvard sources.

items.title: Indus (Harappan) script
items.note: Undeciphered sign system of the mid-third millennium BCE; status as writing and possible cuneiform influence uncertain (Woods 2010). Perspectives needed on the linguistic versus non-linguistic debate; seals from Harappa and Mohenjo-daro (UNESCO WHC 138).

items.title: Proto-Elamite script
items.note: Undeciphered script of Susa and the Iranian plateau, c. 3100 BCE, possibly inspired by proto-cuneiform (Woods 2010). Under-recorded region for this period.

items.title: Clay tokens and sealed envelopes (bullae) of the Late Uruk period
items.note: Some 130 excavated envelopes, about 80 intact; Chogha Mish envelopes CT-scanned at the Oriental Institute; Schmandt-Besserat token theory versus Amiet/Zimansky/Woods critiques. Sources: sites.utexas.edu/dsb, Visible Language ch. 2.

items.title: Tam Pà Ling cave, Laos
items.note: TPL 1 U-series dated 63.6 ± 6 ka, but O'Connell et al. 2018 argue the remains were redeposited into 40–50 ka sediments. Mainland Southeast Asia is under-recorded; look for the Demeter et al. papers and later re-dating of the site (open access PNAS/Nature Communications likely).

items.title: Jebel Faya, Sharjah
items.note: Levallois, blade and bifacial tools dated ~125–130 ka (MIS 5e), basis of the 'Jebel Faya model' of an early southern dispersal across Arabia (Groucutt et al. 2015, PMC6715448). Arabia is thin in the atlas; pair with the Nubian/'beaked' Levallois sites in Oman and the humid-phase (Green Arabia) climate record.

items.title: Galla Placidia
items.note: Woman at the centre of western politics: captive of Alaric's Goths in 410, wife of Athaulf and of Constantius III, regent for Valentinian III; mausoleum at Ravenna. Birth year approximate and must be sourced; DIR has a Galla Placidia entry to start from.

items.title: Draining of the Mesopotamian marshes and displacement of the Maʿdān (Marsh Arabs)
items.note: ICOMOS evaluation of WHC 1481 notes archaeological study during the draining and that the nomination gives no detail on the Marsh Arabs; Indigenous/non-elite people under-recorded. Needs UNEP and HRW sources; audience_note.

items.title: Proto-Elamite script at Susa
items.note: duplicate of -3099-proto-elamite-script

items.title: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Khufu
Carving of the Great Sphinx of Giza
Heit el-Ghurab (settlement of the Giza pyramid builders)
Logbook of Merer (Wadi al-Jarf papyri A and B)
Wadi al-Jarf, harbour of Khufu on the Red Sea
Memphis and its Necropolis (Old Kingdom capital)
Aspasia of Miletus
items.note: Milesian non-citizen woman, partner of Pericles; their son was granted citizenship after the plague killed Pericles' legitimate sons (FHW Pericles page). SEP's Socrates entry also names her as a teacher figure. A woman whose status shows the limits of the 451/450 BCE citizenship law; birth year is approximate and must be sourced.

items.title: Flight of enslaved people from Attica during the Spartan occupation of Decelea
items.note: SEP's Socrates chronology notes that the Spartan fort at Decelea (from 414/413 BCE) encouraged Athenian slaves to escape; Thucydides 7.27 gives the ancient figure. Centres enslaved people, many of them mine workers; verify date and numbers against Thucydides and scholarship.

items.title: Maronea silver strike and the building of the Themistoclean fleet
items.note: Ath. Pol. 22.7: silver at Maronea yielded 100 talents and, on Themistocles' proposal, paid for 100 triremes that fought at Salamis. Link to enslaved labour in the Laurion mines (Akrigg via Kellogg: >30,000 male slaves for mines and navy). Check the archon-year conversion (Nicomedes, 483/2 BCE).

items.title: Lamian War
items.note: Stub child of this record. Diodorus 18.8–18 (Geer Loeb, LacusCurtius) with the editor's chronological notes: Amorgos, Crannon (Dinsmoor: 5 September 322 BCE), Antipater's 2,000-drachma franchise, >12,000 removed, ~9,000 retained, Macedonian garrison.

items.title: Nok culture of central Nigeria
items.note: duplicate of -0500-nok-culture-iron-metallurgy

items.title: Lady Six Sky (Ix Wak Chanil Ajaw) of Naranjo
items.note: Dos Pilas princess who arrived at Naranjo in 682 (Naranjo Stela 24) and acted as regent for K'ak' Tiliw Chan Chaak; died 741. Key study: Helmke 2017, Contributions in New World Archaeology 11:83–130. Naranjo site coordinate on GeoNames (17.133511, -89.262047). Woman ruler; under-recorded.

items.title: Lady Yohl Ik'nal, ruler of Palenque (583–604)
items.note: One of very few Classic Maya women to rule in her own right for a full term (21 years); Kaan attack of 599 on Palenque in her reign. Skidmore 2010 Rulers of Palenque (Mesoweb), after Martin and Grube 2008.

items.title: Arrival of Sihyaj K'ahk' at Tikal (Teotihuacan entrada)
items.note: 8.17.1.4.12 11 Eb 15 Mak (Jan 378; 14 or 16 Jan Gregorian by 584283/584285). Stuart 'Arrival of Strangers' (Mesoweb), Tikal Stela 31, Naachtun Stela 24 (mayadecipherment.com), conquest vs. other readings as perspectives; Spearthrower Owl.

items.title: Defeat of Tikal in the star war of 562
items.note: Caracol Altar 21 (dedicated 633 by K'an II); start of the ~130-year Tikal Hiatus; victor contested (Caracol's Yajaw Te' K'inich II vs. Kaan ruler Sky Witness, Martin 2005 PARI Journal 6(1)).

items.title: Terminal Classic Maya collapse
items.note: c. 800–1000 CE; drought (Kennett et al. 2012; Evans et al. 2018 Science; Medina-Elizalde & Rohling 2012), multi-causal human-environment model (Turner & Sabloff 2012 PNAS, PMC3435155), warfare (Canuto et al. 2018). ~90% population decline in central lowlands.

items.title: Calakmul (seat of the Kaan dynasty)
items.note: UNESCO WHC 1061 (2002, extended 2014); 120 stelae; Kaan capital moved from Dzibanché; Structure II; needs model (footprint, phases).

items.title: Ankhhaf, vizier and director of works under Khufu
items.note: Khufu's half-brother, in charge of Ro-She Khufu per the Merer logbook (Tallet 2017); his bust is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (verify).

items.title: Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan
items.note: Spec 6.4 model-first list names Tenochtitlan's Templo Mayor. Phases I–VII (López Luján 2019, Mesoweb PDF), 78 × 83.6 m base, ~45 m high, materials by rock type; INAH Museo del Templo Mayor pages; Coyolxauhqui find 21 Feb 1978; Tlaltecuhtli monolith and cuauhxicalco (2011). Needs its own model record with stage-by-stage footprints.

items.title: Toxcatl massacre at the Templo Mayor
items.note: Pedro de Alvarado's attack on Mexica nobility during Toxcatl, May 1520 (23 May per Kruell; mid-May per Olivier, UNAM Noticonquista). Spanish testimony (1521 Velázquez inquiry, 1529 residencia) versus Nahua accounts (Florentine Codex Book 12, Anales de Tlatelolco, Códice Aubin). Calendar of the 23 May date needs checking; no reliable death toll. audience_note required.

items.title: Siege and fall of Tenochtitlan
items.note: Siege of ~93 days (Bernal Díaz, Gutenberg #32475) ending with Cuauhtémoc's capture 13 Aug 1521 Julian = 23 Aug Gregorian. Brigantines on Lake Texcoco, Tlaxcalan and other Indigenous allies, famine and disease. Needs the Nahua perspective (Florentine Codex Book 12) and casualty ranges with provenance.

items.title: Tlatelolco
items.note: Twin city and great market of the Mexica, absorbed by Tenochtitlan in 1473 (Bueno Bravo 2005, REAA 35). Zona Arqueológica de Tlatelolco (OSM 19.4513, -99.1377); last stand of 1521; later Colegio de Santa Cruz where Sahagún's Nahua collaborators worked. Year set to the sourced 1473 absorption; its own founding date needs sourcing.

items.title: Formation of the Aztec Triple Alliance
items.note: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan ally after defeating Azcapotzalco (Smith 2017, REAA 47); indirect rule over conquered city-states; Itzcóatl and Tlacaélel's rewriting of official history (Excélsior 2019; INAH Boletín 360). Polity polygon needed for the ambient layer.

items.title: Smallpox epidemic in central Mexico, 1520
items.note: 5–8 million deaths (Acuna-Soto et al. 2002, EID 8:4); Bernal Díaz traces it to a man in Narváez's company; killed the tlatoani Cuitláhuac. Thread: smallpox from Egypt to Tenochtitlan to eradication 1980 (spec 7 example). Florentine Codex Book 12 imagery of the sick.

items.title: Chinampas of Xochimilco
items.note: Part of UNESCO WHC 412; Ramsar site 'Sistema Lacustre Ejidos de Xochimilco y San Gregorio Atlapulco'; Indigenous raised-field agriculture still farmed. Year set to the contact-era landscape UNESCO describes; archaeological dating of chinampa origins still needed.

items.title: Xiongnu
items.note: Steppe empire centred on Mongolia, c. 209 BCE to the late 1st century CE (Lee et al. 2023, Science Advances, PMC10104459, opened). Han accounts are hostile outsiders' views; centre archaeology and aDNA (Egiin Gol, Takhiltyn Khotgor, Shombuuzyn Belchir elite women's burials). Primary region is Mongolia, which the M49 list folds into eastern_asia; decide and justify.

items.title: Zhang Qian
items.note: Life path Chang'an – Xiongnu captivity – Ferghana – Sogdiana – Bactria – return c. 13 years later; marquis of Bowang 123 BCE; tomb at Chenggu, Hanzhong (UNESCO 1442 component, N33 09 32 E107 17 28). Hirth 1917 translation on Silk Road Seattle; Shiji 123 / Hanshu 61. Birth year unknown: use death c. 114 BCE only if sourced. His Xiongnu wife and companion Gan Fu deserve mention.

items.title: Cai Lun presents improved papermaking to the Han court
items.note: Hou Hanshu 78 (Yuanxing 1 = 105 CE; bark, hemp, rags, nets). Perspective: Western Han paper at Fangmatan (Gansu, c. 2nd c. BCE map fragment) and Xuanquan posthouse; dispute over whether these are true paper (Xinhua 2016, HK Museum of History 1998). Starts the paper thread toward Samarkand (751 tradition) and Gutenberg. Find a peer-reviewed fibre-analysis paper.

items.title: Ban Zhao
items.note: Woman historian and court scholar who completed parts of the Hanshu after her brother Ban Gu's death and wrote Lessons for Women (Nüjie). Under-recorded woman; sources thin online — look for university-press translations (Nancy Lee Swann 1932) and Hou Hanshu 84 Biographies of Women. Dates c. 45–c. 117 CE need sourcing.

items.title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
items.note: Hou Hanshu 8: Zhonghe 1, 2nd month, Zhang Jue of Julu, followers claimed 360,000, simultaneous rising; He Jin appointed. Religious movement (Way of Great Peace) as belief; casualties unknown — say so. Loewe (CHC 1) treats it as the real end of Han authority. Needs audience_note.

items.title: Han conquest of Nanyue and the commanderies of northern Vietnam
items.note: Emperor Wu's annexation of the Nanyue kingdom (capital Panyu, modern Guangzhou; Nanyue King's tomb museum) and the commanderies of Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Rinan; later Trưng sisters' rising (40–43 CE) as a linked Vietnamese-centred target. Verify 111 BCE date; South-East Asia is under-covered.

items.title: Roman sack of Epirus and enslavement of its population (167 BCE)
Tribunate and killing of Tiberius Gracchus (133 BCE)
Kingdom of Numidia
items.note: Amazigh (Berber) kingdom of Masinissa, whose war with Carthage in 150 BCE triggered the Third Punic War; Jugurtha; annexation under Caesar. Under-recorded North African polity; Medracen and Cirta as places.

items.title: Monte Verde archaeological site
items.note: Los Lagos, Chile (UNESCO Tentative List 1873, coords 41°30'17" S, 73°12'16" W). MV-II ~14,500 cal BP (Dillehay et al. 2015, PMC4651426) versus mid-Holocene 8,200–4,200 BP (Surovell et al. 2026, Science doi:10.1126/science.adw9217) and the May 2026 eLetter rebuttals. Strongly contested; needs perspectives. Place kind, importance likely 3 or more, so a model is needed (structure footprint from Dillehay's excavation reports).

items.title: White Sands human footprints (Locality 2)
items.note: Bennett et al. 2021 (Bournemouth author manuscript), Pigati et al. 2022 reply and 2023 pollen/OSL study, Oviatt et al. 2022 Quaternary Research critique; USGS data releases 10.5066/P9ABZEM9 and 10.5066/P9E36U4B; NPS footprint pages (sloth-stalking trackway, woman-and-child trackway of 2018).

items.title: Anzick-1 (Clovis infant burial, Montana)
items.note: Named archaeological individual: site 24PA506, Park County; 10,705 ± 35 14C BP (12,707–12,556 cal BP); red ochre, ~100 stone and 15 osseous Clovis tools; genome (Rasmussen et al. 2014, PMC4878442); tribal consultation and requested reburial. Handle respectfully; check reburial outcome in later sources.

items.title: Clovis complex
items.note: 13,050–12,750 cal BP from 32 dates at 10 sites (Waters et al. 2020, PMC7577710); short versus long chronologies; the Clovis-first model and its abandonment; Clovis end and proboscidean extinction.

items.title: Fishtail (Fell) projectile point complex of South America
